thread.title: From Amazon to Apple, October's swoon has erased trillions from America's biggest companies. Here's who's down the most in Pittsburgh

author: Jeff Jeffrey
title: From Amazon to Apple, October's swoon has erased trillions from America's biggest companies. Here's who's down the most in Pittsburgh
text: – National Digital Producer, The Business Journals, Oct 30, 2018, 1:53pm EDT October has been a rollercoaster ride for America's largest companies, with even the healthiest corporate titans racking up tens-of-billions in lost market value since the month began. A Business Journals analysis of the nation’s largest 5,000 public companies determined roughly $3.2 trillion in market capitalization was lost between Oct. 1 and Oct. 29, as uncertainties concerning trade, interest rates and economic instability abroad sent U.S. stock markets swooning. The 30 public companies in the Pittsburgh region examined lost a total of $25.36 billion in value during October, with only one company avoiding a drop in value this month. The largest percentage drops were by Ampco-Pittsburgh, losing 38 percent of market cap so far in October, EQT Corp., losing 32 percent and ExOne, down 31 percent. To see how all the local companies fared, click on the image above. The ranking starts with the one company not losing market value in October and ends with the company with the largest market cap loss this month, a loss of more than $6.5 billion. Nationwide, Amazon (Nasdaq: AMZN) suffered the biggest hit to its market capitalization, defined as the total trading value of its stock outstanding, shedding roughly $224.5 billion since October began. The drop lowered Amazon’s market cap by roughly 23 percent to $752.5 billion as of the close of trading Oct. 29. Other technology giants were among the biggest losers for the month. Google-parent Alphabet (Nasdaq: GOOG) dropped 14 percent, shedding $120.5 billion in value to close with a market cap of roughly $714.2 billion as of Oct. 29. That was second worst among all U.S. companies analyzed, followed by Microsoft's (Nasdaq: MSFT) $79.8 billion decline (off 9 percent), a $65.2 billion (down 6 percent) decline by Apple Inc. (Nasdaq: AAPL) and a $64.6 billion drop (off 14 percent) for Facebook Inc. (Nasdaq: FB). The falloff in market cap comes amid steep volatility in U.S. stock markets. As of the stock closes of Friday and Monday, the stock slide had erased all of the year-to-date gains logged by the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500. Both indices closed below their values of Jan. 2, 2018, each of the past two days.
